headline: UK Bill Puts EU Agreements Before Parliament
deck: A Commons debate and expected vote on 7 December concern a bill that would enable the food-and-drink and emissions agreements to be implemented.
body: Britain's government introduced the Cutting Costs (European Partnership) Bill, which it says would put its food-and-drink and emissions agreements with the European Union into UK law. [E1] The bill would enable implementation of a sanitary and phytosanitary agreement and an emissions-trading-system linking agreement. [E2]

A common UK-EU food-safety area would remove paperwork for imports and exports, the government says. [E3] It says the bill would end export-health certificates costing up to £200 each and remove "Not for EU" labels from most products. [E4] About £6.5 billion of British exports, including steel and aluminium, would be exempted from the EU carbon adjustment mechanism, the government says. [E5]

Targeted alignment with EU food and carbon rules is part of the arrangements, and the bill would establish formal parliamentary scrutiny of new and updated rules, the government says. [E6] ITV News reported that MPs would get their first say on Andy Burnham’s EU deal the following month. [E7] ITV News also reported that the House of Commons will debate the implementing legislation on 7 December, with a vote expected to follow. [E8] Ministers say most British exporters already meet the bloc’s standards, ITV News reported. [E9]

source_note.raw_excerpt: British businesses will see lower trading costs, less paperwork, and renewed access to European markets as the government introduces the ‘Cutting Costs’ (European Partnership) Bill to Parliament today From: Cabinet Office and The Rt Hon Hamish Falconer MP Published: 26 November 2026 ‘Cutting Costs’ Bill to be introduced in Parliament today to put landmark UK-EU food & drink and emissions agreements into UK law. Legislation will save industry millions by cutting red tape, lifting bans on iconic British exports, and exempting £6.5 billion of British exports from EU carbon taxes. Britain has secured legally binding decision-shaping rights, ending years of British businesses following EU rules without a say just to trade with our largest market. British businesses will see lower trading costs, less paperwork, and renewed access to European markets as the government introduces the ‘Cutting Costs’ (European Partnership) Bill to Parliament today (Thursday 26 November).
